Plan: review in batches, package code (jaxfne/) before scripts/ before tests/ before tutorials/examples, since jaxfne/ is the highest-leverage surface (public API + core simulation logic). For each file: (1) read it, (2) run/identify its associated test(s) if any and capture real pass/fail counts (no tail-truncated runs -- see meta_corrections for why that's unsafe), (3) write purpose/score/tbi/tbd/warnings/evidence following the same evidence-based standard as the 16 already-reviewed entries, (4) set last_verified to the actual review date. Do not batch-assign scores without reading each file -- a fabricated number is explicitly called out in the schema description as worse than an honest null. Suggested batch order: jaxfne/core.py submodules and jaxfne/fields/ first (largest, most-depended-on), then jaxfne/vis/ (18 files, partially spot-verified already), then jaxfne/optim/, then scripts/evidence_figures/ (large but lower-risk, used for release receipts not runtime correctness), then tests/ and tutorials/examples last. items.title: step_sdr_transform/step_gsdr_transform/step_agsdr_transform docstrings claim distinct algorithms but are byte-identical plain gradient descent
items.shape: Docstrings claim delta rule / genetic deselection / adaptive GSDR respectively, but all three functions are identical plain gradient descent (u_t - eta*grad_l). Same public names (SDR/GSDR/AGSDR) resolve to two unrelated implementations depending on entry point -- a real correctness/discoverability risk, not yet verified end-to-end which entry point production code actually uses.

items.title: compile_connection_rules_jax builds a dense O(n_pre*n_post) grid via jnp.tile, contradicting sparse-first design
items.shape: Confirmed via direct read this session (jaxfne/connectivity.py:452-476): pre_grid/post_grid are materialized via jnp.tile to full (n_pre, n_post) shape BEFORE probability-masking and max_edges truncation -- a real dense O(n_pre*n_post) memory/compute pattern. Only call site found is tests/test_v0341_kernels.py (1 test) -- the production sparse path is the separate compile_connection_rules (non-_jax suffix), so this is a lower-traffic public API, not on the hot path, but it IS exported in __all__ and contradicts jaxfne-harden-sparse-connectivity doctrine if a user calls it at scale (e.g. 10k x 10k = 100M elements, several hundred MB). Fix: either rewrite to sample sparsely (segment-based or rejection sampling without the dense intermediate), or add an explicit docstring warning about O(n^2) memory scaling if rewriting is out of scope.
items.source: jaxfne/optim+vis-adjacent batch-review agent finding, independently re-verified via direct Read this session

items.title: run_stdp_stream applies @jax.jit to a closure (run_chunk_scan) redefined fresh inside the per-chunk for-loop
items.shape: Confirmed via direct read this session (jaxfne/streaming.py:115-137): the for chunk_idx in range(n_chunks) loop defines a fresh @jax.jit-decorated run_chunk_scan function object on every iteration. jax.jit caches by function identity by default -- a new function object per iteration means a new compile target per chunk, i.e. N_compile likely scales with n_chunks, directly violating this repo doctrine recompilation is the silent killer; assert N_compile <= 1. Not yet trace-verified with an actual compile counter (e.g. via runtime_report() or a jax compile-count hook) -- that verification is the next step before claiming the severity, since JAX may still cache by trace signature in some cases. Fix if confirmed: hoist run_chunk_scan definition outside the loop, parameterize via static_argnums or closures over loop-invariant values only. VERIFICATION ATTEMPTED 2026-06-30, INCONCLUSIVE: tried to count actual XLA compile events via a real run (3 vs 6 vs 1 chunk) with stderr logging capture, but the JAX version installed in this env did not emit log lines matching the expected "Compiling jit(run_chunk_scan)" pattern (0 matches across all chunk counts, including with the dtype bug in my test harness fixed). This does NOT confirm the code is fine -- it means my logging-based detection method did not work in this JAX version, not that no extra compiles happened. The static-code finding (fresh function object defined per loop iteration, no static_argnums/cache hoisting) remains true regardless and is still the real concern. Next attempt should use jax.jit(...).lower(...).compile() with an explicit per-call object identity check, or jax.clear_caches() + a hit-count monkeypatch on jax.jit itself.
items.source: jaxfne/optim+vis-adjacent batch-review agent finding, independently re-verified via direct Read this session -- NOT yet trace-verified for actual recompile count

brainstorm.description: 2026-06-30: repo-wide AST scan for function-merger candidates (pattern: y1=f1(x1), y2=f2(x2), same output identity, incomparable inputs -> merge into y3=f1(x1,x2)). Method: parsed all 387 .py files via Python's ast module, extracted every function/async function with an EXPLICIT return type annotation (1182 functions; unannotated functions excluded -- no fabricated type inference), grouped by exact annotation string match. 96 distinct return types were shared by 2+ functions; most are false positives (coincidental generic types like dict[str, str]/Any/bool shared by unrelated functions). Verdict on the strongest candidates, each individually checked against actual source, not just the type-match heuristic:
brainstorm.real_candidate: build_model/apply_drive_correction -> Model: jaxfne/hdp_network.py's OWN docstring claims it consolidated this exact duplicate pattern from 2 older scripts, but scripts/hdp_1000_neuronal_tensor_column.py, scripts/hdp_suite2_visualizations.py, and scripts/spectrolaminar_tfne_izhikevich_pipeline.py still have their own un-migrated copies the original consolidation missed. Tracked as planned item merge-build_model-apply_drive_correction.
brainstorm.already_solved_confirmed: construct(cfg_or_tensor, runtime=None) in core.py is ALREADY the merged form of the Configuration-path and NeuronalTensor-path Model construction (dispatches via isinstance) -- this is the user's exact merge pattern, already implemented, not a gap.
brainstorm.investigated_and_rejected: simulate_edge_recurrent_izhikevich{,_homeostatic,_hdp,_receptor_exponential} (4 kernels, same output shape) -- this is the exact five-way dispatch problem already audited in this session's Phase 2 work and confirmed NOT cleanly mergeable (different jax.lax.scan carry shapes per mode).
false_positives_confirmed: load() vs load_neuronal_tensor(): load_neuronal_tensor is already a literal 1-line compat alias of load() -- not a duplicate.
EmitterState.initial_state/step (x2 each): two classes implementing the same Protocol/interface -- intentional polymorphism, not duplication.
module-level run_trials/run_receipt vs Model.run_trials/run_receipt methods: standard free-function + thin-delegating-method pattern already used throughout this codebase, not duplicated logic.

step_{agsdr,gsdr,gsgd,sdr}_transform (4 optimizer steps, identical signature): inputs are actually COMPARABLE (same shape already), not incomparable -- already a clean strategy pattern behind OptimizerSpec; merging would add indirection without removing real duplication (did not verify internal logic for true duplication, only the signature).
brainstorm.limitation: Only functions with explicit `-> Type` annotations were scanned (1182 of an unknown larger total). Functions relying on inferred/implicit return types are NOT covered by this pass -- absence from this analysis does not mean a function has no merge candidate, only that it wasn't checked.
